claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children do you have, and what are their names?**

This will help me understand your family situation and assess eligibility for each child.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex is 16 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know you have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old and living with you.

To assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather a bit more information about your circumstances.

**Could you tell me: Is Alex still in full-time education, or has Alex left school?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has left school - they're not in any education at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

**Could you tell me: Is Alex currently in paid work or employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Could you tell me: Are you currently receiving any benefits related to Alex, such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, or income-based Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**One final question: Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK? Also, do you currently reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

Based on the circumstances you've described:
- Alex is 16 years old
- Alex has left school and is not in full-time education
- Alex is not in paid work or employment
- You are not receiving Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, or income-based Employment and Support Allowance
- You reside in the UK

Unfortunately, under the Child Benefit rules, eligibility ends when a child reaches age 16, unless they are in full-time education, an apprenticeship, or certain other specific circumstances apply. Since Alex has left school and is not in full-time education or an apprenticeship, and is not in paid work, Alex would not qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. However, if Alex's circumstances change - for example, if they enter full-time education, an apprenticeship, or start paid work - you may wish to reapply, as their eligibility status could change depending on their situation.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
